questions.question: _____ uses a network of sensors to monitor the vibration levels in the structures such as bridges and buildings.
questions.explanation: Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) uses embedded sensors to continuously monitor structural integrity — detecting vibrations, stress, cracks, and potential failures in infrastructure like bridges and buildings.

questions.question: Number of layers in NGN (Next Generation Network) architecture is ______.
questions.explanation: NGN architecture has 4 layers: Access Layer, Transport Layer, Control Layer, and Service Layer — providing a modular, flexible network framework.

questions.question: Media Gateways are located in ________ of NGN.
questions.explanation: Media Gateways reside in the Access Layer of NGN — they convert media formats between different network types (e.g., PSTN voice signals to IP packets). This conversion allows traditional telephone networks to communicate seamlessly with modern IP-based networks.

questions.question: IoT stands for _____.
questions.explanation: IoT = Internet of Things — a network of physical devices embedded with sensors, software, and connectivity to exchange data over the internet.

questions.question: The _____ provide the connectivity for communication and generally support functions within the NGN.
questions.explanation: Transport functions in NGN provide the core connectivity infrastructure for communication — handling data transfer across the network backbone. They ensure reliable, high-speed movement of voice, video, and data between access points and service platforms.

questions.question: _____ wireless technology is used to deliver higher multi-Gbps peak data speeds.
questions.explanation: 5G technology delivers multi-Gbps peak data speeds (up to 20 Gbps theoretically) — enabling ultra-fast downloads, low latency, and massive device connectivity.

questions.question: The IEEE stands for ________.
options: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineering
Institute of Electronic and Electrical Engineers
Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers
Institute of Engineering and Electronics Engineering
questions.correctText: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers
questions.explanation: IEEE = Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers — the world's largest technical professional organization, developing standards for networking, electronics, and computing.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a characteristic of IoT?
questions.explanation: AI is not a core IoT characteristic. IoT devices are self-configuring, have unique identities, and self-adapting — but AI is an enhancement, not a defining feature.

questions.question: IEEE 802.11 is a collection of __________ communication standards.
questions.explanation: IEEE 802.11 is the family of WLAN (Wireless LAN) communication standards — commonly known as Wi-Fi. It includes variants like 802.11a (5GHz), 802.11b/g (2.4GHz), 802.11n (Wi-Fi 4), 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5), and 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6), each improving speed and efficiency.

questions.question: This _______ provides the alignment interface between the soft-network and the PSTN signaling network.
questions.explanation: Signaling Gateways bridge IP-based networks and traditional PSTN signaling (SS7) — enabling communication between soft-switches and legacy telephone networks.

questions.question: ______ protocols determine how the data is physically sent over the network's physical layer or medium.
questions.explanation: Link layer (Data Link Layer) protocols define how data is transmitted over the physical medium — handling framing, error detection, and MAC addressing.

questions.question: Wi Max, Wi-Fi, LTE technology is used in ______ mobile network.
questions.explanation: WiMax, Wi-Fi, and LTE are 4G technologies — providing high-speed mobile broadband with IP-based architecture and data rates up to 100 Mbps (LTE) to 1 Gbps (LTE-Advanced).

questions.question: Architecture of blockchain is bpm in the year _______.
questions.explanation: Blockchain architecture was introduced in 2008 by Satoshi Nakamoto in the Bitcoin whitepaper — revolutionizing decentralized, trustless transactions.

questions.question: The block which has no previous block or reference is called __________.
questions.explanation: The Genesis Block is the very first block in a blockchain — it has no previous block reference (previous hash is typically zeros) and is hardcoded into the blockchain software. All subsequent blocks are cryptographically linked back to this foundational block.

questions.question: The first block of blockchain is called as ______.
questions.explanation: The first block in any blockchain is called the Genesis Block — it serves as the foundation upon which all subsequent blocks are built. It is unique because it is the only block that does not reference a previous block, and is typically embedded in the software itself.

questions.question: How many layers are there in Blockchain architecture?
questions.explanation: Blockchain has 5 layers: Application Layer, Semantic Layer, Execution Layer, Consensus Layer, and Network Layer — each serving distinct functions.

questions.question: Nodes is defined as a ________.
options: A computer in a Blockchain network
questions.correctText: A computer in a Blockchain network
questions.explanation: A node is any computer participating in the blockchain network — maintaining a copy of the ledger, validating transactions, and following consensus rules.

questions.question: Bitcoin and Ethereum are examples of _______.
questions.explanation: Bitcoin and Ethereum are cryptocurrencies — decentralized digital currencies using cryptography for security and blockchain for transaction verification.

questions.question: Where is Blockchain's central server?
questions.explanation: Blockchain has NO central server — it's distributed across all participating nodes, making it decentralized and resistant to single points of failure.

questions.question: In __________ layer of blockchain, simple instructions or set of multiple instructions in the form of smart contract are executed?
questions.explanation: The Execution Layer in blockchain is where smart contracts and simple instructions are processed and executed. It takes the rules defined in the Semantic Layer and actually runs them — handling transaction validation, state changes, and computation on the network.

questions.question: Write the correct sequence steps of procedure to Establish the Chain of Custody?
questions.explanation: Chain of Custody: 1) Label original materials, 3) Take screenshot of evidence, 4) Install bit-by-bit copy to forensic computers, 2) Perform hash test to authenticate working copies.

questions.question: Which of the following are the considerations involved with digital evidence?
options: Consider safety of personnel at the scene
questions.explanation: Digital evidence handling requires all considerations: clear terminology, documenting extra steps, and personnel safety — ensuring proper evidence integrity and admissibility.

questions.question: EMCI means _______.
questions.explanation: EMCI = Extended Model for Cyberspace Investigation — a comprehensive framework for conducting systematic digital investigations. It extends traditional forensic models to address the unique challenges of cyberspace, including volatile evidence, jurisdictional issues, and cross-border investigations.

questions.question: In IDIP Model which phase requires an investigator to walk through the physical crime scene and identify pieces of physical evidence?
questions.explanation: In the IDIP (Integrated Digital Investigation Process) Model, the Survey phase requires investigators to physically walk through the crime scene, identifying and documenting potential evidence. This crucial step ensures nothing is overlooked before detailed collection begins.

questions.question: ADFM stands for ______?
questions.explanation: ADFM = Abstract Digital Forensic Model — a theoretical framework providing a structured, generalized approach to digital forensic investigations. It defines common processes across different forensic models, helping standardize investigation methodologies regardless of specific tools or environments.

questions.question: Contacts with inmates are examples of ______?
questions.explanation: Testimonial Evidence includes statements from witnesses, informants, or contacts — verbal or written accounts provided by individuals with knowledge of the case. In digital forensics, this can include interviews with suspects, testimony from network administrators, or statements from cybersecurity personnel.

questions.question: The general ethical norms for investigator is _____.
options: To contribute to society and human being
questions.explanation: Investigators must follow all ethical norms: contributing to society, upholding evidence integrity, and maintaining confidentiality throughout investigations.

questions.question: The ________ says that an original writing must be offered as evidence unless it is unavailable, in which case other evidence of its contents may be used.
questions.explanation: The Best Evidence Rule requires that original documents or records be offered as evidence in legal proceedings — copies are acceptable only if originals are unavailable, destroyed, or inaccessible. In digital forensics, this means producing the original digital file or a bit-for-bit forensic image, not just a summary.

questions.question: Documented evidence is same as ________ where the proof is presented in writing?
questions.explanation: Documented/Demonstrative evidence presents proof in tangible form — documents, records, diagrams, or physical exhibits used to support claims.

questions.question: Identify the missing step in the following from Executing the Ethical Hacking process: 1. Start by getting adequate background information about your organization... 2. Narrow down your scope. Pinpoint the specific systems you are targeting.
options: Proceed to the implementation of appropriate countermeasures as recommendations from the findings.
Narrow your focus more, coordinate with IT staff, and conduct research to obtain detailed facts.
Pull down specialized software that identifies exploitable vulnerabilities or assessment tools could incorporate these results.
questions.correctText: Narrow your focus more, coordinate with IT staff, and conduct research to obtain detailed facts.
questions.explanation: After scoping, ethical hackers must narrow focus further, coordinate with IT staff, and research detailed facts before proceeding to vulnerability assessment.

questions.question: The intent of ethical hacking is _________.
options: to discover the hackability of the organization
to promote the malicious attacker's hack tool to better secure systems.
to discover vulnerabilities from a malicious attacker's viewpoint to better secure systems.
to introduce vulnerabilities into the global internet.
questions.correctText: to discover vulnerabilities from a malicious attacker's viewpoint to better secure systems.
questions.explanation: Ethical hacking aims to find vulnerabilities from an attacker's perspective — enabling organizations to fix weaknesses before malicious hackers exploit them.

questions.question: Using password cracking algorithm to gain access to a system is an example of ______.
questions.explanation: Password cracking to gain system access is classified as System Hacking — it directly targets authentication mechanisms to compromise a system. This involves techniques like brute force attacks, dictionary attacks, or rainbow tables to bypass login controls and obtain unauthorized access.

questions.question: The intent of _______ is to validate that security controls exist using a risk-based approach.
questions.explanation: Ethical hacking (security assessment) validates existing security controls using a risk-based methodology — ensuring controls are effective and properly implemented.

questions.question: Nmap is a(n) ________.
options: widely used commercial freeware, and open source network security scanner.
automated tool used for hacking, auditing, and discovering hosts on a network.
questions.correctText: widely used commercial freeware, and open source network security scanner.
questions.explanation: Nmap (Network Mapper) is a free, open-source network security scanner — widely used for port scanning, service detection, OS fingerprinting, and network discovery. Security professionals and ethical hackers use it to map network topology and identify open ports and running services on target systems.

questions.question: Respecting privacy is a ________.
questions.explanation: Respecting privacy is a legal and ethical obligation during security assessments — assessors must protect any sensitive data or personal information they encounter. This obligation ensures that vulnerability testing does not compromise individual privacy rights or expose confidential organizational data.

questions.question: Ethical Hacking is _________.
options: Identifying weaknesses in computer systems and/or computer networks and coming up with countermeasures that protect the weaknesses.
Identifying weaknesses in programmer and coming up with countermeasures that protect the weaknesses.
Identifying weaknesses in only software and attacking the same.
Enhancing the weakness in computer system.
questions.correctText: Identifying weaknesses in computer systems and/or computer networks and coming up with countermeasures that protect the weaknesses.
questions.explanation: Ethical hacking identifies vulnerabilities in systems/networks and develops countermeasures — protecting organizations by fixing weaknesses proactively.

questions.question: This symbol (Grey Hat) signifies _______.
options: White hat hacker, a hacker who gains access to system with a view to fix identified weaknesses.
Gray hat hacker, a hacker who is in between ethical and black hat hackers.
Black hat hacker, a hacker who gains unauthorized access to computer systems for personal gain.
Hacktivist, a hacker who uses hacking to send social, religious, and political etc. messages.
questions.correctText: Gray hat hacker, a hacker who is in between ethical and black hat hackers.
questions.explanation: Grey Hat hackers operate between ethical (white) and malicious (black) hacking — sometimes violating laws but without malicious intent, often disclosing vulnerabilities publicly.

questions.question: Searching through trash cans and dumpsters for intellectual property, passwords, network diagrams, and other information means _________.
questions.explanation: Dumpster diving is a physical social engineering technique — searching trash for discarded documents, passwords, or sensitive information that wasn't properly destroyed.

questions.question: Vulnerability scanning in ethical hacking finds _________.
questions.explanation: Vulnerability scanning identifies weaknesses (vulnerabilities) in systems — security flaws, misconfigurations, or missing patches that could be exploited by attackers. Automated scanners like Nessus or OpenVAS compare system states against known vulnerability databases to produce actionable reports.

questions.question: Built in authentication system of a College exam portal is broken down and passwords are cracked to gain access- this attack comes under _________.
questions.explanation: Attacking a web portal's authentication system is an Application Attack — targeting software vulnerabilities in web applications rather than OS or network infrastructure.

questions.question: Windows attack leads to ___________.
options: Capturing and modifying confidential information as it travels across the network
questions.explanation: Windows attacks often aim to gain remote control of workstations — exploiting OS vulnerabilities to take over systems for further exploitation.

questions.question: How are the Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities exploited?
options: The attackers alter backend SQL statements by manipulating the user-supplied data.
They try to target scripts embedded in a page that are executed on the client-side browser rather than at the server side.
By hacking an email server or performing a basic banner grabbing...
They attack two or more users on the same or different e-mail systems that have autoresponder configured.
questions.correctText: They try to target scripts embedded in a page that are executed on the client-side browser rather than at the server side.
questions.explanation: XSS attacks inject malicious scripts into web pages that execute in victims' browsers — stealing cookies, session tokens, or performing actions on behalf of users.

questions.question: What is traffic analysis or social network analysis?
options: Gathering messaging-related information via log files or network analyzer that can tell the attacker about conversations...
Capturing information while it travels across the network. For example, password stored on servers and workstations.
Gathering internal network configuration information, such as hostnames and IP addresses.
questions.correctText: Gathering messaging-related information via log files or network analyzer that can tell the attacker about conversations...
questions.explanation: Traffic analysis examines communication patterns — who communicates with whom, when, and how frequently — revealing relationships and sensitive information without accessing content.

questions.question: To prevent attachment-overload attacks what should be done?
options: Limit the size of operating system files
Limit the size of either e-mails or e-mail attachments.
Limit the number of users in the network
questions.correctText: Limit the size of either e-mails or e-mail attachments.
questions.explanation: Attachment overload attacks flood systems with large email attachments. Limiting email/attachment sizes prevents storage exhaustion and service disruption.

questions.question: Which one amongst the following is a network infrastructure vulnerability:
options: Any unauthorized employee gaining access to the passwords of system
A malicious employee using a network analyzer can steal confidential information in e-mails and files sent over the network.
A malicious employee gaining authentication to enterprise system files causing changes in most files.
An authorized user entering into network for low level work in exchange for money.
questions.correctText: A malicious employee using a network analyzer can steal confidential information in e-mails and files sent over the network.
questions.explanation: Network sniffing/analysis attacks exploit network infrastructure vulnerabilities — capturing unencrypted data in transit across the network. A malicious insider using a network analyzer (like Wireshark) can intercept emails, files, and credentials, making encryption and network segmentation critical defenses.

questions.question: ______ is a technique used by hackers to find the information exposed accidentally to the internet.
questions.explanation: Google Dorking uses advanced search operators to find accidentally exposed information — sensitive files, login pages, cameras, and vulnerabilities indexed by search engines.

questions.question: Attackers can use _______ running on your network to make their systems appear as your system.
questions.explanation: ARP spoofing/poisoning allows attackers to associate their MAC address with a legitimate IP — intercepting, modifying, or redirecting network traffic.

questions.question: DoS refers to ________ attack.
questions.explanation: DoS = Denial of Service attack — an attack that floods a target system with overwhelming requests or traffic, exhausting its resources (CPU, memory, bandwidth) so legitimate users cannot access the service. Common targets include web servers, DNS, and email systems.

questions.question: Attachment overloading attack, connection attack, autoresponder attack are understood as _____.
questions.explanation: Email bomb attacks include attachment overloading, connection attacks, and autoresponder loops — flooding email systems to cause denial of service.

questions.question: Which port is used for Telnet?
questions.explanation: Telnet uses Port 23 for remote terminal access — transmitting data (including passwords) in cleartext, making it insecure compared to SSH (Port 22).

questions.question: Banner Security tip for SMTP server is _____.
options: Make sure that you're always running the latest software updates.
Make sure that you're always changing the network IP.
Make sure that you're always changing password.
Make sure that you're removing the person and title info.
questions.correctText: Make sure that you're always running the latest software updates.
questions.explanation: Keeping SMTP servers updated with the latest patches is critical — closing known vulnerabilities that attackers could exploit through banner grabbing or direct attacks.

questions.question: Storage overload and bandwidth blocking can cause ______.
questions.explanation: Message Overloading Attacks consume storage and bandwidth by flooding systems with excessive messages — causing denial of service. When email servers are overwhelmed with massive volumes of messages, storage fills up and bandwidth is consumed, disrupting legitimate communication.

questions.question: _______ is a form of internet abuse which is perpetrated through the sending of massive volumes of email to a specific email address...
questions.explanation: Email bombing floods a specific email address with massive volumes of email — overwhelming the inbox, consuming server storage, and potentially causing the entire mail system to crash. This denial-of-service technique can also be used to distract victims from more targeted attacks happening simultaneously.

questions.question: As an attacker, you should scan all ________ UDP and ________ TCP ports on each network host that's targeted by your scanner.
questions.explanation: Both UDP and TCP have 65,535 possible ports each (numbered 0-65535). Comprehensive port scanning checks all possible ports on target systems to discover every running service — while well-known ports (0-1023) are most commonly targeted, attackers also scan ephemeral ports for hidden services.

questions.question: Attack to find two or more users on the same or different e-mail systems that have autoresponder configured can be understood as _________.
questions.explanation: Autoresponder attacks exploit auto-reply loops between two email addresses that both have auto-responders configured — creating endless reply cycles that consume bandwidth, fill storage, and disrupt mail services. Each auto-response triggers another, creating an infinite loop of messages.

questions.question: When the hacker corrupts data within the heap, and that code change forces your system to overwrite important data, it is called as ________.
questions.explanation: Heap-based buffer overflow attacks corrupt dynamically allocated memory (the heap) — overwriting critical data structures and potentially executing arbitrary code. Unlike stack-based overflows that target return addresses, heap overflows manipulate program data structures, making them harder to detect but equally dangerous.
